receipt.public_excerpt: 77% of employees using AI say these tools have added to their workload, and nearly half (47%) of employees using AI report they do not know how to achieve the expected productivity gains.

evidence_items.explanation: In a survey of full-time employees in four countries (April-May 2024), most employees who use AI said it added to their workload. That is a negative work experience shared by many ordinary workers.

evidence_items.locator: section 'Do workers find AI chatbots helpful for their work?', paragraph 1

receipt.public_excerpt: Among workers who have used AI chatbots for work, 40% say these tools have been extremely or very helpful in allowing them to do things more quickly. A smaller share (29%) say they have been highly helpful in improving the quality of their work.

evidence_items.explanation: In October 2024, most US workers who had used chatbots such as ChatGPT did not rate them as highly helpful for speed (60%) or quality (71%). That is far from universal enthusiasm.

evidence_items.locator: section 'Why some workers have not used AI chatbots for work', paragraph 2

receipt.public_excerpt: Among workers who are not AI chatbot users, 36% say a major reason they have never used AI chatbots for work is that there isn’t any use for them in their job.

evidence_items.explanation: Pew found that 69% of workers did not use chatbots at work. Of those non-users, over a third said a major reason is that the tools have no use in their job. This shows widespread indifference outside the enthusiast groups.

evidence_items.locator: section 'Do workers find AI chatbots helpful for their work?', paragraph 5

receipt.public_excerpt: Among workers who use AI chatbots regularly, 54% say they’ve been highly helpful in speeding up their work and 41% say they’ve been highly helpful in improving their work quality.

evidence_items.explanation: Counterevidence: a meaningful share of workers, especially regular users, found chatbots highly helpful. So positive views were not confined to coders. This tempers the claim but does not refute 'much of the outside world feels differently'.

unresolved_gaps: Neither survey separates coders or tech enthusiasts from other workers, so the contrast Marcus draws is not measured directly.
Upwork's '77% added to workload' measures extra workload, not overall dislike. Some of those workers may still value the tools.
The Microsoft/LinkedIn 2024 Work Trend Index reports that 90% of AI users say it saves time. It could not be quoted cleanly, and it samples knowledge workers who already use AI.
